Parliament No:11
Session No:1
Volume No:82
Sitting No:18
Sitting Date:07-03-2007
Section Name:BUDGET
Title:HEAD K - MINISTRY OF EDUCATION
MPs Speaking:Dr Lam Pin Min;Dr Lily Neo;Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Marine Parade);Dr Ong Seh Hong;Mdm Cynthia Phua (Aljunied);Mdm Ho Geok Choo (West Coast);Mr Abdullah Tarmugi;Mr Alvin Yeo (Hong Kah);Mr Chan Soo Sen (Joo Chiat);Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah);Mr Gautam Banerjee (Nominated Member);Mr Hri Kumar (Bishan-Toa Payoh);Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Marine Parade);Mr Matthias Yao Chih;Mr Michael Palmer (Pasir Ris-Punggol);Mr Ong Kian Min (Tampines);Mr Siew Kum Hong (Nominated Member);Mr Abdullah Tarmugi (Mr Speaker);Mr Wee Siew Kim (Ang Mo Kio);Mr Yeo Guat Kwang (Aljunied);Mrs Jessie Phua (Nominated Member);Mrs Josephine Teo (Bishan-Toa Payoh);Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar);Ms Lee Bee Wah (Ang Mo Kio);The Minister for Education (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam);The Minister of State for Education (Mr Gan Kim Yong);The Minister of State for Education (RAdm (NS) Lui Tuck Yew);The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Community Development, Youth and Sports (Mr Teo Ser Luck);The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman);The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M);The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)

Column No : 3060

 

     Head K - Ministry of Education

 

          The Chairman:  Head K - Ministry of Education.  Dr Lily Neo.

 

Future Students

 

     Dr Lily Neo: Sir, I beg to move,

 

    That the total sum to be allocated for Head K of the Estimates be reduced by $100.

 

   Sir, it is imperative that our greatest resource, our people, is well-equipped to meet the demands of a rapidly evolving and globalised world. The essential task of MOE is to ensure that our citizens are equipped with the knowledge, skills and qualifications they need to participate in this new economy.  Creativity, flexibility and innovation are key tools we need to survive and compete in this new knowledge-based economy.

 

    Education can no longer stop after one leaves school or even college. Individuals must take it upon themselves to constantly improve and upgrade.  It is not MOE's role to do so, but it can help prepare students to be lifelong learners and steer Singapore to be a learning society. The vision is to build a new culture of learning that will underpin national competitiveness and personal prosperity,

 

 

encourage creativity and innovation and help build a cohesive society.

 

12.45 pm

 

     MOE could encourage and make it conducive, rewarding, and non-disadvantageous for citizens to continue learning throughout their lives, not just in the years of compulsory schooling.  As a start, MOE could begin at the primary level, and prepare our students to cultivate the habit of lifelong learning.  MOE could, in its teaching guidance, help nurture the following perceptions in children, to continue the evolution towards a more fully realised embrace of motivation to learn.

 

     MOE could, for example, adopt the recommendations of the UNESCO Delors Report which highlighted four pillars of education:

 

     (1)  Learning to know.  This involves the mastery of learning tools rather than the acquisition of structured knowledge.  It includes developing concentration, memory skills and the ability to think.
